query: What pilot sample size, duration, and success criteria (data completeness %, inter-rater kappa threshold, dashboard latency target) are appropriate for a 3-month pilot?

response.query: What pilot sample size, duration, and success criteria (data completeness %, inter-rater kappa threshold, dashboard latency target) are appropriate for a 3-month pilot?
response.answer: For a 3-month pilot, aim for a sample size of 30-50 participants, 80% data completeness, inter-rater kappa ≥ 0.7, and dashboard latency ≤ 2 seconds.

results.title: The retrospective chart review: important methodological ...
results.content: :   The retrospective chart review (RCR), also known as a medical record review, is a type of research design in which pre-recorded, patient-centered data are used to answer one or more research questions [1]. :   Attesting to the popularity of this technique, a review of three emergency medicine journals revealed that nearly one-quarter of all research published within the study’s timeframe used RCR methodology [3]. In sum, in instances where researchers have access to multiple sites or plan to study a common disorder or medical procedure, random sampling is the preferred method. | Create well-defined, clearly articulated research questions   Consider sampling questions *a priori*   Operationalize variables included in retrospective chart review   Train and monitor data abstractors   Develop and use standardized data abstraction forms   Create a data abstraction procedure manual   Develop explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria   Address inter-rater and intra-rater reliability   Conduct a pilot test   Address confidentiality and ethical considerations |.
